KR.read: Korea's hair care now has a domestic size anchor: IMARC puts the market at US$1.8bn for 2025 (RETAIL, LOW confidence), forecast to US$2.4bn by 2034. That sits alongside the existing trade picture — total Korean hair-care exports (HS 3305) of US$0.413bn (EXPORT_FOB, HIGH, UN Comtrade, 2024), of which US$0.003bn went to India ([CORRIDOR]-tagged).
KR.trend: A growth_yoy figure now exists but is a projection, not an observed rate: derived from two adjacent Mordor Intelligence forecast values (US$1.32bn 2025 to US$1.39bn 2026), it works out to +5.3% (ESTIMATE confidence) — consistent with the same source's own 5.42% CAGR (2026-2031) and roughly 2pp hotter than IMARC's separate forecast CAGR of 3.23% (2026-2034, LOW), which also disagrees with Mordor on level (a 1.36x gap). No observed KR growth_yoy is on file for the domestic market; the reliable observed figures remain on the export side.
KR.caveats: The domestic size is a single LOW-confidence aggregator estimate; the HIGH-confidence figures are exports (EXPORT_FOB), a different basis that cannot substitute for domestic retail scale.

IN.read: India's hair-care market is sized at US$4.1bn (RETAIL/MRP-inclusive, LOW, Mordor, 2026), with a 'skinification' shift toward actives and serums. Sub-segment detail is now firmer: shampoo ~US$1.26bn (2025), and scalp_care captured through three conflicting proxy measures (alopecia US$267mn, hair serum US$155mn, hair-growth products US$825mn) that reflect how differently 'scalp care' is scoped. India also imported US$0.199bn of hair-care products from the world (US$0.031bn from China) (IMPORT_CIF, HIGH, UN Comtrade, 2024).
IN.trend: A growth_yoy figure now exists but is not independently observed: derived from two consecutive Market Research Future values (US$4,100mn 2024 to US$4,287.37mn 2025), it works out to +4.57% (ESTIMATE confidence) — numerically identical to MRF's own 4.57% forecast CAGR on the same page, since the 2025 value is modelled off that rate rather than separately measured. A forecast CAGR of 4.73% (2026-2031, LOW, Mordor) sits close to it, while IMARC's separate 10.58% (2026-2034, LOW) implies a much faster trajectory on the same market — none of these is an observed rate. The scalp-care/serum sub-space is where the 'skinification' momentum sits, but its size proxies are LOW and definitionally scattered.
IN.caveats: Segment and sub-segment figures are LOW-confidence aggregator estimates from different houses on different definitions; the three scalp-care measures are not comparable to each other, and organised/unorganised coverage is unstated.

combined.read: Both markets now carry RETAIL value_usd_bn sizes, so a directional comparison holds: India (~US$4.1bn, LOW) is roughly 2x Korea's domestic hair care (~US$1.8bn, LOW), though both are single LOW-confidence estimates. The corridor angle is thin in absolute terms — Korea's hair-care exports to India are just US$0.003bn ([CORRIDOR]), consistent with AmorePacific's Mise En Scène and RYO being recent (2025) Nykaa entrants rather than established sellers — while India separately imports US$0.199bn of hair care from the world (IMPORT_CIF, a different basis, not netted). The shared structural story is 'skinification': actives-led scalp/serum demand is the growth edge in both markets, and the clearest near-term corridor opportunity.
